conclusion: The described check-then-act interleaving is constructible if crate-private reservation methods are called independently on cloned Arcs, but the audited current production ownership order prevents its prerequisite old physical_returned from overlapping old negative_stop. No source change is necessary solely for that hypothetical call pattern in this batch.
ownershipEvidence: The only non-test production caller of physical_returned is RuntimeOwner::poll(&mut self), after physical_thread::is_finished on the original HTTP JoinHandle and its subsequent join. shared.returned additionally requires completed Net/native/Hub destruction.

The HTTP thread owns the StartPlan reservation clone and calls negative_stop only while run() is live. That thread must finish all such calls before its kernel thread signals and UI poll may release the claim.

UI request_stop_at takes &self on the unique non-Clone RuntimeOwner; safely running poll(&mut self) on that same value concurrently is excluded by Rust borrowing. Sharing RuntimeOwner through a Mutex serializes those calls; sharing Arc<RuntimeOwner> does not yield &mut poll while outstanding shared references exist.

The public StartPlan and RuntimeOwner do not expose their reservation Arc or fields. WebRuntimeReservation and its methods are crate-private. Current UI State owns one Option<RuntimeOwner>; no clone/Arc of a reservation is supplied to another independent worker which can call physical_returned.

Drop/recover_retained transfers the original non-Clone owner through a single retained slot; it does not duplicate a live HTTP thread or permit concurrently polling two RuntimeOwners for one reservation.
limits: This is a closed-world source call-site/ownership audit, not a claim that the private atomic methods are generally linearizable under every independently constructed schedule.

The P2 caveat remains valid documentation for a future internal caller change: adding independent concurrent physical_returned/negative_stop would need exact-epoch readiness or serialization and regression evidence.
